0x0034D6: A development program for assault-type humanoid mobile weapons. A twin pillar to the <SRX Project>, it builds machines that largely forgo <EOT>, per the wishes of its head, Dr. Marion Radom. Originally aimed at the Federation's next mainline unit, it now develops custom machines for ace pilots.
0x0036B6: A plan to develop special humanoid weapons for anti-alien combat. Units like the R-Series apply <EOT> extensively.
0x003787: One type of 'barrier' - defenses that nullify enemy attacks. It directly projects non-physical energy: EM waves, gravity, telekinesis, photons, etc. Fields are matched to the attack, working by neutralization, diffusion, compression, cancellation, distortion, etc. Airborne matter may crystallize on the field's surface, seeming to 'shatter' when it fails.
0x003A04: Short for Mass Amplitude Preemptivestrike Weapon: a weapon for mass wide-area first strikes. MAPWs divide by area of effect into straight-line, circular, and impact-scatter types. Also called 'map weapons.'
0x003B88: The conflict caused by the Aerogaters after the <DC> War, in New Era 187. Based on Neviim (codename: White Star), an automated planetoid that suddenly appeared at L5, the Aerogaters raided the Earth Sphere with insectoid mobile weapons such as the Megillot. Impressed by humanity's combat skill, they schemed to make humans their own soldiers, but lost in the final battle, Operation SRW. They were later found to be humans mentally conditioned by an unknown party - a fact kept strictly secret.
0x003F05:
The first fully sealed space colony, completed in New Era 075. It houses the Colony Integrated Government and the headquarters of the <Colony Integration Army>. Colony history through the 180s was one of hardship: civil strife in 076 after the space-adaptation surgery given to the first emigrants failed; a terrorist bid for autonomy in 157 (the Nozomi Incident); a bulkhead bombing in 172 (the Hope Incident); and a BC-weapon attack in 184 (the Elpis Incident), each costing many lives.
From the early 160s, the NID4 movement sought self-rule from the Earth Federation Government by peaceful means. Its leader, Brian Midcrid, won over Earth's public opinion, achieved independence in 184, and became the first president; the Federation space forces stationed there became the <Colony Integration Army> under supreme commander Maier.
The ten colonies, all at L4, are No. 1 Elpis, No. 2 Nozomi, No. 3 Hoffnung, No. 4 Wish, No. 5 Espoir, No. 6 Hope, No. 7 Space, No. 8 Esperanza, No. 9 Speranza, and No. 10 Nadezhda.
0x004659: A man-machine interface developed by Egret Feff, a scientist at the giant hibernation facility, the <Earth Cradle>, with Adler's backing. It direct-links pilot and machine for smoother control, and can also act on the pilot from the machine side, forcibly boosting aggression and reaction speed. At present, pilots cannot endure prolonged use without undergoing some form of enhancement.
